data.name: Florinius
data.gender_notes: Florinius is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Florinius is of Latin origin and translates to 'Flowering, Abundant, Prosperous'. This name was often given to those who were prosperous or had a flourishing life, and was also given as a nod to the Roman god Florus, who represented prosperity and the fruits of the earth. In Christian tradition, Florinius is the name of a martyr who was beheaded in Africa during the Roman persecutions. He is remembered for his faith and courage in the face of persecution, and is often invoked as a patron saint of farmers, gardeners, and those in need of prosperity and abundance.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes prosperity, growth, and the blessings of nature.

in_hebrew.name: פלוריניוס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: פלוריניוס הוא שם שנגזר מהבסלט, florin, שמשמעותו נוצר, גדל, חי. על פי המסורת, זהו שם מאשר, שהוטבע על ידי מלאך. בעברית, זוהי צורה של שם עברי, פלור, שמשמעותו פרח, והסופית -יוס, המציינת אדם. בתרבות העברית, זהו שם שמסמל חיים ואור.

in_greek.name: Φλογενιός
in_greek.long_meaning: Φλογενιός (Φλογενιός) είναι ονομασία που προέρχεται από τη λέξη φλογη (φλόγα), που σημαίνει φλόγα και θερμός. Είναι μια από τις πρώτες ονομασίες που προέρχονται από την αγγελία του Χριστού από τον αρχάγγελο Γαβριήλ. Η λέξη φλογη σημαίνει φωτισμός, φωταγωγή, και θερμότητα, και είναι συνδεδεμένη με την αντίληψη της Θείας Φλόγας. Σε ιστορικό και θρησκευτικό πλαίσιο, η ονομασία Φλογενιός συμβολίζει την κληρονομιά του Χριστού και την αγγελία του.

in_latin.name: Florinius
in_latin.meaning: nomen: flos, flower, floresco, florere, florens
in_latin.long_meaning: Florinius, nomen Christianum, originem habet a radicibus flor-, significans florem, florere, floresco, florens. In antiquitate, Florinus fuit unus ex primis nominibus qui fuerunt attributi sanctis. Florinus significat flores, qui est symbolum vitae, speranza, et felicitas. In historia Ecclesiae, Florinus est unus ex nominibus qui fuerunt datum sanctis a primo seculo. Nomina Florinius, Florinus, et Flores sunt synonyma, omnia significans florem, et omnia significans virtus, et felicitas.

historical_references.reference: The Roman emperor Florian was born around AD 211 in the province of Pannonia Inferior (modern-day Hungary). He was a military man who rose to prominence during the chaos following the death of Emperor Alexander Severus in AD 235. Florian was a devout Christian and was martyred for his faith during the persecutions under Emperor Valerian in AD 276.

Saint Florian of Lorch was a Christian martyr in the late 3rd or early 4th century AD. He was a Roman soldier stationed in the town of Lorch (modern-day Austria) and was martyred for refusing to offer sacrifice to the Roman gods. According to legend, Florian was tortured and then placed in a barrel with pitch and set on fire. He survived the ordeal, but was later beheaded.
